context: Add a 'key_id' part to _SECRET_KEY_PARTS (it normalizes to 'keyid' and would then match s3_key_id, aws_key_id, key_id). Check the existing platform-options tests for any key that would newly redact and would be a behavior change worth calling out.
description: is_secret_option_key() in benchbox/core/results/platform_options.py normalizes keys by stripping non-alphanumerics and matches against _SECRET_KEY_PARTS, which includes 'access_key' but not 'key_id'. So s3_key_id normalizes to 's3keyid' and is NOT redacted, and an explicit --platform-option s3_key_id=AKIA... reaches exported result metadata verbatim. Companion keys are covered: pg_password -> 'pgpassword' matches 'password', s3_secret -> 's3secret' matches 'secret'. Low severity - an AWS access key ID is an identifier rather than the secret half of the pair - but it is still credential material in published data.

preserves.behavior: Already-redacted keys (password/token/secret/...) keep their current behavior
Non-secret option keys still export their real values
